<reason>Side B won by anchoring its case in the motion's core constraint—finite land in land-scarce cities—and systematically dismantling Side A's alternatives. After Side B exposed that plot recycling and mausoleums violate the very religious covenants Side A sought to defend, Side A retreated to reserving "dedicated sections" for in-ground burial. Side B then boxed Side A in with pressure questions, forcing Side A to concede in Rebuttal 2 that when those sections fill, cities must either seize other urban land or "coordinate with peri-urban religious cemeteries"—the exact out-of-town solution Side A had previously attacked as an unjust travel burden and "private exile."</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side B's first rebuttal [B2.1-B2.2] and closing follow-through [B5.1-B5.3]: Side B showed that Side A's proposed land-management tools (such as lease-based plot recycling) required exhuming the dead in violation of the religious covenants Side A championed, and later caught Side A conceding reliance on the very peri-urban cemeteries it had condemned in [A2.6].</best_rebuttal>
